whoWeAre.label: Who We Are
whoWeAre.title: A Software Studio With Real Business Domain Expertise
whoWeAre.intro1: Nordic Riser AB is a Stockholm-based software studio. We design and build multilingual web platforms, secure client portals, and custom products for businesses that operate in more than one language, currency, or jurisdiction — including our own products, like Global Reach and NR-BOS.
whoWeAre.intro2: What sets us apart is where we started: advising international entrepreneurs on establishing compliant business structures in Europe. That consulting practice is still active today, and the domain knowledge it gives us — regulatory thinking, cross-border operations, institutional-grade documentation — goes into every platform we build.
whoWeAre.mission: “To build software that works the way cross-border businesses actually operate — and to bring real business expertise to every platform we ship.”

software.title: Software & Products
software.body: Multilingual web platforms, secure client portals, custom products, and workflow automation — for clients, and for ourselves.

consulting.title: Consulting
consulting.body: Business establishment and cross-border advisory for international entrepreneurs — our original practice, still active today.

whyWeExist.label: Where We Started — Our Consulting Practice
whyWeExist.title: Built to Address a Genuine Gap in International Advisory
whyWeExist.sub: Before we were a software studio, we recognised that too many internationally minded professionals were navigating complex European business and relocation processes without access to structured, professional-grade strategic support.
problemParagraphs: International entrepreneurs and professionals often encounter fragmented advice — generic information that fails to account for their specific business model, professional background, or long-term objectives. The result is poor planning, avoidable delays, and structures that do not withstand institutional scrutiny.

Nordic Riser AB was established to change this. We bring a consulting firm's rigour to what is often an unstructured process — delivering clarity, documentation, and professional coordination at every stage.
Our focus is always on long-term strategy and sustainable outcomes, not short-term convenience.

pillars.title: Long-Term Strategy
pillars.body: We design structures that serve your business objectives over time, not just immediate requirements.

pillars.title: Full Legal Compliance
pillars.body: Every recommendation is grounded in current regulatory frameworks and institutional standards.

pillars.title: Structured Business Solutions
pillars.body: We provide documented, systematic processes — not informal guidance or general information.

pillars.title: Professional Consulting Standards
pillars.body: Our engagements are managed with the discipline and accountability of a professional services firm.

approach.label: Our Consulting Approach
approach.title: Strategy First. Structure Always. Compliance Throughout.
approach.sub: The same rigour we bring to consulting engagements — assess first, design the structure, execute with care — shapes how we scope and build software too. Below is how it plays out in a consulting engagement specifically.

items.title: Strategy Before Action
items.body: We assess your specific situation thoroughly before making any recommendations. Strategic clarity is the foundation of every successful engagement.

items.title: Legal Structure by Design
items.body: We identify the appropriate legal and corporate framework for your circumstances — entity type, jurisdiction, and compliance obligations are determined systematically.

items.title: Professional Guidance Only
items.body: We do not offer generic information. Every recommendation is specific, documented, and grounded in professional consulting practice.

items.title: Execution with Licensed Partners
items.body: Implementation is coordinated with qualified legal, accounting, and specialist professionals — ensuring technical accuracy and regulatory compliance at every step.

items.title: Long-Term Business Focus
items.body: We measure success by the sustainability of the structures we help create — not by the volume of engagements we process.

items.title: Transparent Communication
items.body: We provide honest, realistic assessments. We do not overstate what is achievable, and we communicate requirements clearly at every stage.

values.label: Our Values
values.title: The Principles That Guide Our Work
values.sub: These are not aspirational statements. They are the operational standards by which every engagement is managed.

items.title: Compliance First
items.body: Every process we design is built to withstand institutional scrutiny. Lawfulness is non-negotiable — it is the baseline from which all strategies are developed.

items.title: Transparency
items.body: We communicate honestly — about requirements, timelines, and realistic outcomes. We do not make promises about decisions that rest with third parties or authorities.

items.title: Structured Process
items.body: Every engagement is documented and managed systematically. Ad hoc advice is not what we provide — structured methodology is.

items.title: Professional Partnerships
items.body: We maintain working relationships with qualified legal, tax, and specialist professionals — ensuring that technical and regulatory aspects are handled with appropriate expertise.

items.title: Confidentiality
items.body: Client information is handled with rigorous standards of discretion. Personal and commercial data is treated as strictly confidential throughout every engagement.

items.title: Tailored Advice
items.body: We do not apply template solutions. Each engagement is assessed individually, and strategy is developed specific to the client's circumstances and objectives.

missionBlock.label: Our Mission
missionBlock.statement: To build multilingual platforms, secure portals, and cross-border products for businesses that operate in more than one language — backed by real business domain expertise, documented processes, and long-term strategic thinking.

s1.title: Introduction
body: Nordic Riser AB (“we”, “our”, or “us”) is committed to protecting your privacy and ensuring the security of your personal information. This Privacy Policy explains how we collect, use, disclose, and safeguard information across everything we operate: this website, our strategic consulting services, the Nordic Riser Member Portal, and the software products we build and license — including NR-BOS and Global Reach.

This policy is designed to comply with the EU General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and applicable data protection legislation. By using our website, our Member Portal, or any of our software products, or by submitting an inquiry, you acknowledge that you have read and understood this policy.

s2.title: Data Controller
intro: Nordic Riser AB is the data controller responsible for your personal information collected through this website, the Member Portal, and our consulting engagements. Section 3 explains the separate case — building and hosting software for a client — in which Nordic Riser AB instead acts as a data processor.
s2.contactNote: For all data protection matters, please contact us using the details above with the subject line “Data Protection Inquiry”.

s3.title: Controller vs. Processor — Which Applies to You
body: Nordic Riser AB relates to personal data in two different capacities, and which one applies depends on what you're using.

As a controller, we decide why and how personal data is processed for our own consulting business, this marketing website, and the Member Portal we operate under our own brand. This Privacy Policy governs that processing.

As a processor, when we build, host, or operate a system on a client's behalf — for example, an NR-BOS deployment run for a construction company's own workforce and clients — the client is the data controller for the personal data in that system, and Nordic Riser AB processes it only on the client's documented instructions, under a Data Processing Agreement. If you are an employee, subcontractor, or client of one of our software customers, this Privacy Policy is not the governing document for how your data is handled there — your relationship is with that customer, and our obligations run to them under the DPA, not directly to you.
We offer a Data Processing Agreement to any client on request — see our Legal index for the DPA.

subheadings.title: 4.1 Information You Provide Directly
subheadings.intro: We collect information that you voluntarily provide to us, including:
list: Contact Information: Name, email address, phone number
Professional Information: Business type, professional background, business objectives
Consultation Request Data: Purpose of consultation and description of your situation as submitted via our contact form
Communication Data: Information contained in emails and other correspondence with our team

subheadings.title: 4.2 Information Collected Automatically
subheadings.intro: When you visit our website, we may automatically collect:
list: Technical Data: IP address, browser type, operating system, device information
Usage Data: Pages visited, time spent on pages, navigation paths
Cookies: Small data files stored on your device (see Section 11)

subheadings.title: 4.3 Member Portal (portal.nordicriser.com)
subheadings.intro: As a registered member, we collect:
list: Account Data: name, email address, authentication credentials, and role, managed through Firebase Authentication
Documents: files you upload for case processing
Messages: the content of secure messages you exchange through the portal
Case & Timeline Data: status and progress information related to your case
Payment Records: invoices, payment claims, and top-up requests you submit — we do not collect or store card numbers; payments are reviewed manually rather than through an automated payment processor

subheadings.title: 4.4 NR-BOS
subheadings.intro: NR-BOS is typically operated by one of our clients for their own workforce, in which case Nordic Riser AB processes this data as a processor, not a controller (see Section 3). We describe it here so that anyone who is a data subject within an NR-BOS deployment understands what is collected:
list: Account & Company Data: the names, roles, and employment relationship of individuals a client organisation adds as NR-BOS users

Worksite Photographs: photographs uploaded through field reports. The photo file is stored exactly as uploaded, including any location or timestamp metadata (EXIF) already embedded by the device that took it. Separately, the field report itself records GPS coordinates and a timestamp reported by the submitting device at the moment of filing, for site-verification purposes. Worksite photographs are never made public — every photo is kept in a private file store and is only ever reachable through short-lived, authenticated links available to authorised members of the relevant project
Project & Task Records: project names, task titles, status, due dates, and assignee
Working Hours: hours logged against tasks by named employees
Cost Data: cost entries associated with projects and tasks

subheadings.title: 4.5 Global Reach
list: Chat Messages: the content of messages sent through Global Reach's live collaboration rooms, including message text submitted for real-time translation — see Section 6.4 for how that translation is provided and Section 7 for the sub-processor involved

s5.title: How We Use Your Information
s5.intro: We process your personal data only for the purposes outlined below, each supported by a lawful basis under GDPR:

rows: Responding to consultation requests and inquiries
Contract performance / Legitimate interest
Providing strategic advisory, technology, and global collaboration services
Contract performance

Contract performance

Contract performance / Consent
Improving our website and service quality
Legitimate interest
Coordinating with third-party professionals (legal, accounting)
Contract performance / Legitimate interest
Compliance with legal and regulatory obligations
Legal obligation

s5.note: We will not sell, rent, or trade your personal information to third parties. We will not use your data for purposes incompatible with those stated above.

subheadings.title: 6.1 Professional Service Partners
subheadings.intro: Where required to deliver our services, we may share relevant information with qualified third-party professionals, including:
list: Legal counsel and specialist advisors engaged in connection with your matter
Accounting and tax professionals involved in business formation or compliance
Technology providers supporting our website, Member Portal, and software product hosting — see our full Sub-processor list, Section 7
subheadings.outro: All third parties are required to maintain appropriate security measures and are permitted to process your data only as directed by us and within the scope of their professional obligations.

subheadings.title: 6.2 Legal Requirements
subheadings.intro: We may disclose your personal information when required to do so by law, regulation, legal process, or a legitimate governmental request.

subheadings.title: 6.3 International Data Transfers
subheadings.intro: Where personal data is transferred outside the EU/EEA, we ensure an appropriate transfer mechanism — typically the European Commission's Standard Contractual Clauses — is in place before any such transfer takes place. Section 7 lists every sub-processor we use, including where each one is located and which transfer mechanism applies. One of those transfers, described in full below, is to a company based in China, a jurisdiction without an EU adequacy decision.

subheadings.title: 6.4 AI Processing in NR-BOS
subheadings.intro: NR-BOS includes an optional AI Assistant that generates risk, cost, and productivity insights from a project's data. We are describing this plainly, including the parts that are not yet as protective as we'd like, rather than describing a safeguard that isn't actually in place:
list: When this feature is used, the relevant project data — including project and company names, budget figures, task details, cost entries, and the full names and roles of assigned team members — is sent to our AI provider, DeepSeek (Hangzhou DeepSeek Artificial Intelligence Co., Ltd.), to generate the analysis.

We do not currently redact or anonymise personal identifiers before this data is transmitted. If this matters to how you use NR-BOS, contact us or your NR-BOS administrator — a client operating NR-BOS as controller can restrict use of the AI Assistant for their own deployment.
DeepSeek's own API data policy states that data submitted through its API is not used to train its models. This is DeepSeek's representation, not a guarantee we independently audit.
The output is advisory only. Nothing in NR-BOS acts on an AI-generated insight automatically — a person always reviews it and decides what, if anything, to do.

Because DeepSeek is based in China, this transfer relies on Standard Contractual Clauses as the GDPR Chapter V safeguard. China has no European Commission adequacy decision, and transfers of this kind are subject to heightened regulatory attention across the EU. We are disclosing this specifically, by name, so that you can decide with full information whether it matters to you — see Section 7 for the full sub-processor entry.

s7.title: Sub-processors
body: To help meet our own transparency obligations and give you full visibility into who processes personal data on our behalf, we maintain a complete, current sub-processor list — what each one does, what data category it touches, where it's located, and what transfer safeguard applies — as its own page, linked from our Legal index.

If we add a new sub-processor, we will update that list and, for clients with a Data Processing Agreement in place, give notice before the change takes effect, consistent with the objection right described in that agreement.

s8.title: Data Security
s8.intro: We implement appropriate technical and organisational measures to protect your personal information against unauthorised access, alteration, disclosure, or destruction. These measures include:
list: Encrypted communication channels for the transmission of sensitive information
Secure server infrastructure and data storage systems
Access controls and authentication procedures for internal systems
Regular review and updating of security practices
Staff awareness of data protection obligations
s8.outro: For the Member Portal, this includes Firebase Authentication together with Firestore and Storage security rules that restrict each user to their own data. For NR-BOS worksite photographs, this includes keeping files in a private object store reachable only through short-lived signed links rather than any public path. While we take all reasonable precautions, no method of electronic transmission or storage is entirely secure. We cannot guarantee absolute security, but we are committed to protecting your data to the highest practicable standard.

s9.title: Data Retention
s9.intro: We retain your personal information only for as long as is necessary to fulfil the purposes outlined in this policy and to comply with our legal obligations:
list: Active Client Data: Duration of the engagement plus 7 years (in accordance with applicable accounting and record-keeping legislation)
Inquiry Data (non-converted): 2 years from the date of last contact
Website Analytics Data: Maximum 26 months

Software Product Data (Member Portal, NR-BOS): retained for the duration of the account or licensing relationship, plus a reasonable period after termination for legal, accounting, and dispute-resolution purposes, unless a shorter period is agreed in a client's Data Processing Agreement
Consent Records: Until consent is withdrawn, plus a reasonable period thereafter for record-keeping purposes
s9.outro: Upon expiry of the applicable retention period, personal data is securely deleted or anonymised.

s10.title: Your Rights Under GDPR
s10.intro: As a data subject under the GDPR, you have the following rights in relation to your personal data:

rights.title: Right of Access
rights.body: Request a copy of the personal data we hold about you.

rights.title: Right to Rectification
rights.body: Request correction of inaccurate or incomplete data.

rights.title: Right to Erasure
rights.body: Request deletion of your data in certain circumstances (“right to be forgotten”).

rights.title: Right to Restrict Processing
rights.body: Request that we limit how we use your data in specified circumstances.

rights.title: Right to Data Portability
rights.body: Receive your data in a structured, machine-readable format where applicable.

rights.title: Right to Object
rights.body: Object to processing based on legitimate interests or for direct marketing purposes.

rights.title: Right to Withdraw Consent
rights.body: Withdraw any consent given at any time, without affecting prior processing.

rights.title: Right to Complain
rights.body: Lodge a complaint with the relevant supervisory authority (see Section 14).

s10.outro: To exercise any of the above rights, please contact us at info@nordicriser.com with the subject line “Data Subject Request”. We will respond within one calendar month as required by GDPR. If you are a data subject within a client's NR-BOS deployment, please direct your request to that client first, since they are the controller for that data — see Section 3.

s11.title: Cookies and Tracking Technologies

subheadings.title: 11.1 Marketing Website (nordicriser.com)
subheadings.intro: This marketing website is a static informational site with minimal tracking. We may use essential cookies required for the basic operation of the site, including remembering your selected language. We do not currently use third-party advertising or behavioural tracking cookies. If we implement analytics or additional tracking technologies here in the future, we will obtain your prior consent before setting any non-essential cookie, disclose its purpose and duration, and offer a straightforward way to withdraw that consent.

subheadings.title: 11.2 Member Portal & NR-BOS
subheadings.intro: The Member Portal and NR-BOS are authenticated applications, unlike the marketing website, and use cookies and equivalent local storage that are strictly necessary for them to function: maintaining your logged-in session, authentication tokens, and security measures such as CSRF protection. These are essential to the service and cannot be disabled without losing the ability to log in. We do not currently use analytics or advertising cookies in the Member Portal or NR-BOS; if that changes, the same consent-first commitment above applies there exactly as it does on the marketing website.

s11.outro: You may control and delete cookies through your browser settings at any time. Please note that disabling essential cookies will prevent you from logging in to the Portal or NR-BOS, and may affect the marketing website's functionality.

s12.title: Children's Privacy
body: Our website, consulting services, and software products are directed exclusively at adults conducting professional and business activities. We do not knowingly collect personal data from individuals under the age of 18. s1.title: Acceptance of These Terms

s8.title: NR-BOS Licensing
s8.intro: NR-BOS is licensed by single-use redemption code, not by subscription billing inside the product. This section describes exactly how that works, matched to how the licensing system actually behaves:

subheadings.title: 8.1 Codes Are Single-Use and Non-Transferable
subheadings.body: Each license code can be redeemed exactly once. Once redeemed, it is permanently bound to the redeeming company and cannot be reassigned, resold, or transferred to a different company or account.

subheadings.title: 8.2 Redemption Extends Your Period
subheadings.body: Redeeming a code adds its duration to your current license period. If your existing period hasn't expired yet, the new period is added on top of it rather than replacing it; if it has expired, the new period starts from the moment of redemption.

subheadings.title: 8.3 No Automatic Renewal
subheadings.body: A license period ends on its scheduled date. Nothing renews automatically — access is paused until a new code is redeemed. There is no recurring billing associated with NR-BOS licensing.

subheadings.title: 8.4 No Refunds on a Redeemed Code
subheadings.body: Once a code has been redeemed, that redemption is final. We do not offer refunds on a redeemed license code, and redemption does not go through a payment processor capable of a reversal — treat redemption as a deliberate, final action.

subheadings.title: 8.5 Revocation
subheadings.body: We can revoke a license code to prevent it from ever being redeemed — this matters if a code is leaked, issued in error, or no longer should be honoured. Revoking a code that has already been redeemed prevents that specific code from being used again, but does not claw back or suspend the access already granted from that earlier redemption. We are stating this precisely because it's a real limitation, not a stylistic choice: at present, we do not have a separate mechanism to suspend a company's already-granted NR-BOS access. If we need to end an active customer's access for cause, we will contact them directly to arrange it rather than relying on a revocation mechanism that isn't built for that.

subheadings.title: 8.6 Trial Codes
subheadings.body: Certain codes are issued as 3-day trial codes. A company may redeem one trial code, ever — a company that has already redeemed a paid (monthly or annual) code is not eligible for a trial code, and a company that has already used a trial code cannot use a second one.

s9.title: Fees & Payment
body: License codes for NR-BOS are issued by Nordic Riser AB following a separate purchase or agreement; the redemption process itself does not collect or process card payment data.
For consulting engagements and Member Portal payment records, invoices are issued and reviewed manually rather than through an automated payment gateway, as described in our Privacy Policy.

Our total liability arising from or relating to these Terms or the Services, for any single claim, will not exceed the amount you paid us for the specific Service giving rise to the claim in the 12 months preceding the event.
Nothing in these Terms limits liability where it cannot lawfully be limited, including liability for death or personal injury caused by negligence, or for fraud.

s11.title: Term & Termination

legalDpa.translationNotice: This page has been machine-translated. In case of any discrepancy, the English version is authoritative. Contact us with questions.
intro: This Data Processing Agreement (“DPA”) applies whenever Nordic Riser AB (“Processor”) processes personal data on behalf of a client (“Controller”) in connection with NR-BOS, the Member Portal, or another Nordic Riser software product, under Article 28 of the GDPR. It supplements — and does not replace — the underlying service agreement or Terms of Service between the parties.
This published version is a template. Contact us to have it executed as a signed agreement referencing your specific engagement.

s1.title: Subject Matter & Duration
body: The subject matter of this DPA is the processing of personal data by the Processor on behalf of the Controller in the course of providing the Services described in the parties' underlying agreement (for example, an NR-BOS license or Member Portal engagement).

This DPA takes effect on the date the underlying service agreement takes effect and remains in force for as long as the Processor processes personal data on the Controller's behalf, including during any post-termination period described in Section 11.

s2.title: Nature & Purpose of Processing
body: The Processor processes personal data to provide, maintain, and support the Services — including hosting, storage, field-report processing, project and task tracking, secure messaging, document exchange, and, where enabled, AI-assisted analysis as described in the Privacy Policy.

The Processor processes personal data only on the Controller's documented instructions, including as set out in the underlying agreement, this DPA, and the Controller's own configuration of the Service (for example, which features are enabled) — unless required to do otherwise by EU or Member State law, in which case the Processor will inform the Controller of that legal requirement before processing, unless that law prohibits such notice.

s3.title: Categories of Data & Data Subjects
body: Categories of personal data processed depend on which Service the Controller uses, and may include: account identifiers and contact details; employment and role information; worksite photographs and associated location/timestamp metadata; project, task, and cost records; logged working hours; uploaded documents; and message content.

Categories of data subjects may include: the Controller's employees, contractors, and subcontractors; the Controller's own clients or customers, where their data is entered into the Service by the Controller; and other individuals whose data the Controller submits in the course of using the Service.

s4.title: Controller's Instructions
body: The Controller instructs the Processor to process personal data to provide the Services, in accordance with the underlying agreement, this DPA, and the Controller's use of the Service's own configuration options.

The Controller warrants that it has a valid legal basis for the personal data it submits to the Service and, where applicable, has provided any notices to or obtained any consents from its own data subjects that its use of the Service requires.

s5.title: Processor Obligations
list: Processes personal data only on the Controller's documented instructions, as described in Section 2
Ensures persons authorised to process personal data have committed to confidentiality
Implements the technical and organisational security measures described in Section 7
Assists the Controller as described in Sections 8 and 9
Does not engage a new sub-processor without providing notice as described in Section 6
Makes available the information necessary to demonstrate compliance with this Article 28 and allows for audits as described in Section 10

s6.title: Sub-processors
body: The Controller gives the Processor general written authorisation to engage the sub-processors listed on the Processor's published Sub-processor list, available on the Nordic Riser AB website.

The Processor will give the Controller notice of any intended addition or replacement of a sub-processor, giving the Controller the opportunity to object on reasonable data-protection grounds before the change takes effect. Every sub-processor is bound by data-protection obligations no less protective than those in this DPA.

s7.title: Security Measures
s7.intro: The Processor implements the technical and organisational measures described in the Privacy Policy's Data Security section, including, as applicable to the specific Service:
list: Encrypted communication channels for the transmission of sensitive information
Authentication and access controls restricting each user to their own data
Private, non-public storage for uploaded files, accessed only via short-lived signed links rather than a public path
Regular review of security practices and staff awareness of data protection obligations

s8.title: Assistance & Data Subject Requests
body: Where a data subject exercises a GDPR right (access, rectification, erasure, restriction, portability, or objection) directly against the Processor concerning data the Processor holds as a processor for the Controller, the Processor will promptly forward that request to the Controller and will not itself respond substantively to the data subject, since the Controller is the appropriate party to respond.

The Processor will provide the Controller with reasonable assistance, taking into account the nature of the processing, to help the Controller fulfil its own obligations to respond to data subject requests and to fulfil its obligations under Articles 32–36 of the GDPR.

s9.title: Personal Data Breach Notification
body: The Processor will notify the Controller without undue delay after becoming aware of a personal data breach affecting the Controller's data, providing the information reasonably available to it to help the Controller meet its own breach-notification obligations under Articles 33 and 34 of the GDPR.

s10.title: Audit Rights
body: On reasonable prior written notice, and no more than once per calendar year unless a personal data breach or a regulatory investigation gives cause for more frequent review, the Controller may request information demonstrating the Processor's compliance with this DPA, and may conduct or mandate an audit of the Processor's relevant processing activities, subject to reasonable confidentiality and scheduling arrangements to avoid disrupting the Processor's operations or other clients' data.

s11.title: Deletion & Return on Termination
body: On termination of the underlying agreement, the Processor will, at the Controller's choice, delete or return all personal data processed on the Controller's behalf, and delete existing copies, within a reasonable period — except to the extent the Processor is required by EU or Member State law to retain some or all of that data, in which case it will continue to protect that data and process it only for the purposes that law requires.

s12.title: Article 28(3) Compliance Statement
body: This DPA is intended to give effect to the requirements of Article 28(3) of the GDPR for the processing described in this document. Where a specific engagement requires additional or different terms — for example, a Controller's own standard DPA, or terms specific to a regulated sector — the parties may agree a supplementary or substitute document in writing; that document will govern to the extent it conflicts with this one.

s13.title: Liability & Governing Law
body: Liability under this DPA is subject to the limitations set out in the Terms of Service between the parties, except where such limitation is not permitted by applicable data protection law.

This DPA is governed by the laws of Sweden, with the Stockholm District Court (Stockholms tingsrätt) as the court of first instance for any dispute arising from it, consistent with the Terms of Service.

hero.label: Consulting
hero.h1: Strategic Consulting for International Business Establishment
hero.body: We provide structured, professional advisory across five core service areas — each designed to support entrepreneurs and professionals building a compliant business presence in Europe.

consulting.servicesSub: Every service we provide is delivered through a structured consulting methodology — assessed individually, documented formally, and coordinated with qualified professional partners where required.

services.title: Business Relocation Strategy Consulting
body: For entrepreneurs and professionals who intend to relocate to Europe through a structured business activity, this service provides strategic planning that begins with your business situation and works forward through the requirements of a legally compliant and institutionally defensible relocation process.

We assess your professional background, business model, and objectives, and develop a documented relocation strategy that integrates business structure, activity requirements, and long-term positioning. Our role is to ensure that every element of your plan is coherent, realistic, and aligned with regulatory frameworks — before any steps are taken.
We do not provide immigration advice or legal representation. We provide the strategic consulting framework from which qualified specialists can operate effectively.

services.title: Company Formation Strategy
body: Establishing a business entity in Europe requires careful strategic planning before any formal steps are taken. The choice of legal structure, jurisdictional considerations, ownership arrangements, and operational setup all have long-term implications — and errors at this stage are difficult and costly to correct.

This service provides structured consulting on how to approach company formation strategically. We help you understand the landscape of available structures, evaluate the most appropriate option for your situation, and develop a formation plan that supports both your immediate operational needs and your long-term business objectives.
Execution is coordinated with qualified legal and accounting professionals who handle the formal registration and compliance work within their licensed capacity.

services.title: Professional Business Plan Preparation
body: A business plan prepared for relocation or business establishment purposes is a formal document that must meet the expectations of European regulatory authorities, financial institutions, and professional reviewers. It is not a marketing document — it is a structured, evidence-based presentation of a viable business model.

We work with clients to develop business plans that accurately represent their activity, demonstrate operational viability, and are structured in line with institutional requirements. The process is methodical: we assess your business model, identify the documentation requirements relevant to your situation, and produce a plan that is coherent, credible, and professionally presented.

All business plans prepared through this service are developed to support formal processes — they are not generic templates, and they are not produced without a full understanding of the client's specific circumstances.

services.title: Freelancer & Entrepreneur Relocation Consulting
body: Independent professionals, remote workers, and small business owners face a distinct set of challenges when planning to establish a legal business presence in Europe. Standard frameworks are often designed with larger entities in mind, and the pathway for a sole trader or micro-business requires a more tailored strategic approach.

This service is specifically designed for freelancers, remote professionals, and early-stage entrepreneurs who are building — or planning to build — a legal and sustainable business base in Europe. We help you understand what a compliant structure looks like for your professional profile, what documentation and planning is required, and how to position your activity credibly within regulatory frameworks.

We assess each client individually. What is appropriate for a software consultant differs significantly from what is appropriate for a creative professional or a product-based entrepreneur — and our advisory reflects that.

services.title: Cross-Border Business Advisory
body: Entrepreneurs who operate across multiple countries face a more complex set of strategic and structural considerations. Questions of where to incorporate, how to manage cross-border transactions, how to structure ownership, and how to remain compliant across jurisdictions require careful and informed analysis — not generic answers.

This service provides advisory for internationally active business owners who need to think coherently about their multi-jurisdictional footprint. We help you map the relevant considerations, identify potential structural conflicts or opportunities, and develop a framework for managing your cross-border business activities in a way that is both operationally practical and compliant.
Where legal, tax, or regulatory specialist input is required — as it often is in cross-border matters — we coordinate engagement with qualified professionals in the relevant jurisdictions.

whoThisIsFor.label: Our Client Profile
whoThisIsFor.title: We Work With Four Distinct Client Groups
whoThisIsFor.sub: Our services are designed for professionals who require structured, compliance-grounded consulting — and who understand that building a business presence in Europe is a process that requires planning, documentation, and professional coordination.

groups.title: Entrepreneurs Planning to Relocate to Europe
body: This group consists of business founders and owner-operators who have decided — or are seriously considering — relocating to Europe through a structured business pathway. They typically have an existing business model or professional activity, and they understand that a credible, institutionally sound relocation strategy must be built on a properly established business foundation.
The challenge for most entrepreneurs in this group is not ambition — it is structure. Our role is to build that structure with them.
groups.challengesHeading: Common consulting needs in this group
challenges: Developing a business plan that meets institutional standards for relocation processes
Selecting the most appropriate legal entity and business structure for their situation
Understanding the regulatory and compliance framework relevant to their business activity
Coordinating legal, accounting, and documentation requirements in a structured sequence
Building a long-term operational strategy for their European business presence

groups.title: Freelancers Working Internationally
body: Independent professionals — consultants, designers, developers, writers, and other knowledge-economy workers — increasingly operate across borders. Many in this group generate consistent professional income and work with international clients, but operate without the legal business structure that a European presence requires.

We work with freelancers to formalise their professional activity into a structured business framework — one that accurately reflects how they work and meets the expectations of European regulatory frameworks.
groups.challengesHeading: Common consulting needs in this group
challenges: Translating freelance activity into a formally structured, documentable business model
Understanding which legal structure is appropriate for a sole trader or micro-business
Preparing professional documentation that demonstrates viable and consistent business activity
Planning a compliant and sustainable path to establishing a legal business base in Europe
Coordinating with relevant legal and accounting professionals for formal registration steps

groups.title: International Professionals
body: This group includes senior professionals, executives, and specialists who are planning to establish long-term business operations in Europe — either as a continuation of their existing professional career or as the foundation for a new phase of their working life.
What they require is a structured consulting framework that translates their professional background into a viable and compliant European business model.
groups.challengesHeading: Common consulting needs in this group
challenges: Structuring professional experience and credentials into a formally viable European business model
Planning a corporate structure suited to long-term professional operations in Europe
Navigating cross-border compliance considerations relevant to their professional activity
Coordinating the documentation and planning required for a structured professional relocation
Establishing a business presence that positions them credibly within their professional sector

groups.title: Small Business Owners Expanding to European Markets
body: Small and medium-sized business owners seeking to expand their operations into European markets face a set of strategic and structural challenges distinct from those of a startup or sole trader.

We help small business owners think through their European expansion strategically — assessing the right entry approach, structuring the legal and operational framework, and coordinating the professional support required.
groups.challengesHeading: Common consulting needs in this group
challenges: Developing a structured European market entry strategy suited to their business model
Selecting and designing the appropriate legal entity for European operations
Integrating a new European structure with their existing business operations and ownership
Managing cross-border compliance and regulatory requirements across jurisdictions
Coordinating legal, tax, and accounting professionals across the formation and setup process

engagementModel.label: Engagement Model
engagementModel.title: What to Expect When You Work With Us
engagementModel.sub: Our engagements follow a structured four-stage process applicable across all service areas.

steps.title: Initial Consultation
steps.body: We conduct a structured assessment of your background, objectives, and constraints. No generic intake forms — a genuine professional conversation to understand your situation.

steps.title: Strategy Development
steps.body: Based on the assessment, we develop a documented strategic framework specific to your circumstances — covering structure, process, timeline, and professional requirements.

steps.title: Documentation & Planning
steps.body: We prepare the required documentation, business plans, or advisory outputs in a format suitable for institutional and professional use.

steps.title: Implementation Coordination
steps.body: We coordinate the implementation phase with qualified legal, accounting, and specialist partners — ensuring the strategy is executed with accuracy and compliance.

packages.label: Engagement Options
packages.title: Ways to Work With Us
packages.sub: Every engagement is scoped individually. The tiers below describe the shape of a typical engagement — final scope and fees are confirmed after your initial consultation.

tiers.name: Initial Consultation
tiers.body: A structured assessment of your situation, objectives, and the most viable pathway forward, with a written summary of recommendations.

tiers.name: Full Engagement
tiers.body: End-to-end strategic support across business structure, documentation, and relocation planning, coordinated with professional partners.

tiers.name: Ongoing Advisory
tiers.body: Continued strategic support after your initial establishment — for evolving business needs, cross-border questions, or expansion planning.

cta.title: Discuss Your Requirements
cta.body: If you are planning to establish a business presence in Europe, we invite you to arrange a consultation. We will assess your situation and provide a clear, structured view of the pathway and services relevant to your objectives.

caseStudies.title: NR-BOS
caseStudies.challenge: Businesses need enterprise-grade operations tooling — project tracking, field reporting, cost control, client reporting — without the cost and complexity of systems like SAP.
caseStudies.build: A subscription-based business operations platform covering projects, task boards, budget tracking, field reports with photo documentation, AI-assisted risk and cost insights, and branded PDF client reports.
caseStudies.result: Live SaaS product, licensed via redeemable subscription codes.

caseStudies.title: Global Reach
caseStudies.challenge: People collaborating across languages lose meaning in translation delays and switching between tools.
caseStudies.build: Live collaboration rooms with shared whiteboards and chat translated in real time between languages, with a freemium entry tier.
caseStudies.result: Live product with a free tier at 100 messages, no card required.

caseStudies.title: Nordic Riser Member Portal
caseStudies.challenge: Advisory clients needed a single place for documents, case status, and communication — with strict access control.
caseStudies.build: Authenticated portal with multi-step onboarding, role-based routing (member vs. admin), document vault, secure messaging, case timeline, and payment centre.
caseStudies.result: Live at portal.nordicriser.com with custom domain and automatic SSL.

caseStudies.title: nordicriser.com
caseStudies.challenge: Reach entrepreneurs across Europe, the Middle East, and South Asia in their own languages.
caseStudies.build: Eleven-language production site with per-language URL structure, RTL support for Arabic and Urdu, full meta and Open Graph coverage, and a GDPR-compliant privacy framework.
caseStudies.result: Every page available in 11 languages with clean, indexable URLs.

caseStudies.title: 4eDoctor
caseStudies.challenge: Patients needed access to medical consultations — with doctors, psychologists, and nurses — without the wait times and friction of in-person visits.
caseStudies.build: A telemedicine platform with HD video and voice consultations, in-call chat, appointment booking, and local payment options.
caseStudies.result: Live product letting patients book and consult a doctor from anywhere, at any time.

caseStudies.title: 4eZone Pharmacy
caseStudies.challenge: Patients with a doctor's prescription had no fast way to get their medicine fulfilled and delivered.
caseStudies.build: A pharmacy fulfillment system linked to doctor prescriptions, with admin dashboards for pharmacies and chemists to process and dispatch orders.
caseStudies.result: Live system connecting prescriptions to pharmacy fulfillment and delivery.

caseStudies.title: On-Demand Delivery App
caseStudies.challenge: Businesses across different industries needed on-demand delivery — ordering, dispatch, and real-time tracking — without building logistics infrastructure from scratch.
caseStudies.build: A customizable delivery platform covering customer ordering, dispatch, and rider tracking, adaptable to different business verticals and available for client projects.
caseStudies.result: A reusable delivery platform ready to be customized and deployed for client businesses.
